title: The family of churches, looking back
tomorrow: is there anything that can come between you and God?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the mystics, inward and at the sink, and Julian's line: all shall be well. Today, a sound: the whole family of churches, singing at once.

Three choirs in one room. One chants, low and steady, the way Orthodox choirs often do. One sings an old Latin hymn. One is a gospel choir that can't keep still. On paper it sounds like a mess. In the room, if they listen to each other, it sounds like a chord. That's the family of churches this path has visited: Orthodox, Catholic, Protestant, many rooms, one house.
screen: `THREE CHOIRS, ONE ROOM.` → `A CHANT, A HYMN, A GOSPEL CHOIR.` → `A MESS, OR A CHORD?`

segments.voice: Paul gives the picture, writing to a church in Corinth that was splitting into camps, each claiming a favorite teacher. “For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” Then the line to tell a friend: “And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee.” Not one sound. Many, needing each other. That's harmony, not unison. The family has real voices. Orthodox Christians, with icons, incense and the Divine Liturgy. Catholic Christians, with the Mass, the saints and the pope. Protestant Christians, in many churches, with the Bible read and preached and hymns sung together. They differ on real things, and they say so: communion, authority, Mary and the saints. Naming those differences honestly is part of loving one another, not a failure of it. And they share real things too. Paul names some in one breath: “One Lord, one faith, one baptism.” On his last night, in John's Gospel, Jesus prays for everyone who will believe later, “That they all may be one.” That prayer is still being prayed in all three rooms.
screen: `ONE BODY, MANY MEMBERS.` · `I HAVE NO NEED OF THEE? NO.` · `REAL DIFFERENCES, NAMED.` · `ONE LORD, ONE FAITH, ONE BAPTISM.` · then, large: `THAT THEY MAY BE ONE.`

segments.voice: Listen for one minute to the sounds around you: a fan, a car, a bird, a voice in another room. Pick them out one by one, and notice how they sit together without becoming one sound. If you pray, pray for the churches by name as the sounds go on: Orthodox, Catholic, Protestant; if not, hold them in mind with good will.
The family of churches. Orthodox, Catholic and Protestant Christians: real differences, one Lord, one body with many members.
Your line: that they may be one. Many voices, one chord: harmony, not unison. See you tomorrow.

Orthodox.meaning: the Eastern family of churches, with icons and ancient liturgy

Divine Liturgy.meaning: the main Sunday worship of Orthodox churches

the Mass.meaning: the main Catholic worship, centered on communion

Protestant.meaning: churches that grew from the Reformation, such as Baptists

icons.meaning: painted images of Christ and the saints, used in prayer
